clue.text: Retire with the magazine section

explanation.surface: Someone retires, taking the supplement from the newspaper with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from something is to quit it; a detachable middle insert in a periodical has the same name.

clue.text: Seclusion results from being awfully hard up

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so these letters come out jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Being terribly short of money leaves a person cut off from society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the letters of HARD UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom of screening women from public view is a form of isolation.

clue.text: Illuminating crossword answers

parts.note: read as lamps that illuminate, and also as the setter's term for the words written into a grid

explanation.surface: A remark that solutions to a puzzle can be enlightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps give illumination, and the entries in a crossword grid are traditionally called by the same name.

clue.text: Where roofers work at management's expense

explanation.surface: Builders on a roof working for free, courtesy of the bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally up on top of a building, and an idiom for something given free by the establishment.

clue.text: Place of imprisonment for thick-headed debtor

indicators.note: the head of the word thick is its opening letter, which is all that is used

parts.note: a debtor is someone who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: A jail for a dim-witted man who cannot pay what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of London held famous prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: The London fortress was long used as a state prison.

clue.text: Rich enough to have gild-edged holdings

explanation.surface: A wealthy person with safe investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gild-edged' stands for gilt-edged: government stocks, often called the Funds in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plenty of money available, and literally holding government securities.

clue.text: One mixed drink not served up in London

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a sling is a cocktail of spirits

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word not is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: A bar in the capital refuses to bring someone a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns NOT into TON. ISLINGTON is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a borough of the British capital, so it lies within the city.

clue.text: Female operations affected men

explanation.surface: Women's surgery has an effect on the men around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandies are men who are vain and showy in dress and manner.

clue.text: He initiates changes when the cytisus reappears

explanation.surface: Someone brings in reforms just as a shrub comes back into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Cytisus is the botanical name for the broom shrub; a fresh one is literally a new one. The proverb says a new broom sweeps clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer eager to reform things is proverbially compared to a fresh sweeping brush; the plant sense gives the second reading.

clue.text: Sea containing a grass so strange

indicators.note: strange implies something odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ocean full of weird weed.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of the North Atlantic is famous for its floating seaweed.

clue.text: Just what one's entitled to

explanation.surface: A plain statement of a person's due.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair or proper, and an entitlement such as a legal claim.

clue.text: Resolve to get a grant of probate

explanation.surface: Determination to obtain official approval of an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength of purpose; and, read as two words, the authority to act on a dead person's testament.

clue.text: The first to be in action

explanation.surface: Someone eager to lead the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In the leading position, and in the forward line of battle.

clue.text: Expert at the front of a sailing boat

indicators.note: the expert word is placed ahead of the letter a

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled sailor standing at the bow of a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay outrigger vessel driven by sail.

clue.text: Biblical verses offering bountiful blessings

explanation.surface: Scripture passages that bring generous blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sermon on the Mount's sayings beginning 'Blessed are', and states of supreme blessedness.

clue.text: Record success for the best father in the world

definitions.text: the best father in the world

explanation.surface: A dad being praised as the finest anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Top of the Pops was a long-running British chart music TV show; 'pops' are fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being first in the music charts; and, playfully, the leading dad of all.

clue.text: Love in my soul is afflicted with foreboding

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: something afflicted is troubled and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lover's soul is troubled by a sense of dread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is afflicted' rearranges O plus IN MY SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a threatening way that hints at trouble to come.

clue.text: The poet who won't strike a weapon carrier

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike

explanation.surface: A pacifist poet carries a weapon nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't strike' suggests violence but means refusing industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath holds a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Personally depicted by an unpaid workman

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A portrait drawn by a volunteer labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn by eye without instruments or tracing, by the artist's own effort.

clue.text: Faith is displayed in its charity

indicators.note: display suggests a new arrangement set out for show, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A belief proves itself by being generous to others.
explanation.definitionFit: The religion of Christ's followers is a creed.

clue.text: Shoot a smuggler

explanation.surface: An order to open fire on a contraband dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's creeping stem that roots, and one who runs illicit goods.

clue.text: Perfect example of how to communicate

explanation.surface: Guidance on ideal communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable instance of something; and, as two words, speech as the means of contact.

clue.text: Wherein BSE inspectors may find cause for complaint

definitions.text: Wherein BSE inspectors may find cause for complaint

parts.words: Wherein BSE inspectors may find cause for complaint
parts.note: meat checked for mad cow disease is also a slang word for a grievance

explanation.surface: Food inspectors discovering a problem in cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease, found in cattle meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle meat where the disease shows, and slang for a grumble.

clue.text: Regards from me

explanation.surface: A letter signed off with kind wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A conventional letter sign-off, and a jocular way of saying oneself.

clue.text: Painter returned last month-clearly in haste!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation is written going back the other way

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the year's final month

explanation.surface: An artist rushes back at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran at speed, hurried.

clue.text: Contra guerrilla concealing a fit of the shivers

indicators.note: the two words conceal the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter in hiding shaking with fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarial fever comes with bouts of shaking.

clue.text: Account containing a single wrong number

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
wrong means the word single is put into a wrong order

explanation.surface: A bill contains one incorrect figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SINGLE into NALGESI with A; 'number' means something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller dulls sensation, making something numb.

clue.text: Died in the attempt to catch a wild animal

explanation.surface: Someone perished trying to trap a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian wild dog.

clue.text: Decrepit stranger comes in duly disheartened

indicators.note: comes in places one word inside the other
taking the heart out of duly leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A frail and peculiar person arrives looking glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' is easily read as gloomy, describing the stranger, but it tells you to drop the middle of 'duly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and feeble from age.

clue.text: Longed to see a knight in action

indicators.note: in places the knight's title within the action word

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Wishing to watch a knight in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanted something keenly.
